doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Buck-and-wing, hucklebuck and tap dancing
summary: Young says he could do the buck-and-wing, hucklebuck and tap routines with the time step and over-the-top.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Buck-and-wing? Yeah, I can do that! I can buck-and-wing, I can do all that, that was very important back in them days, the buck-and-wing. Shoot, and I used to do the…
Yeah, the hucklebuck. [laughs] Yeah, man, I…
Did you tap? Could you tap as well?

I could tap-dance, yeah, time-step. I was a pretty good tap-dancer, yeah, I could do the whole thing. I had a whole routine I could do, the over-the-top and all of that, that‘s the like when you head and your dance, you‘re over-the-top, you know that‘s the end of your thing. Then you dance [sings rhythms]…see, that‘s called over-the-top. That was your last step you would do and you end up, I could do all of that stuff, man. See, I was a good friend to the dancers…what‘s her name…the brothers?
